 Mikel Arteta has been speaking with the press ahead of our trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League.
 Our boss discussed team news, taking on Liverpool and coming up against his compatriot, Andoni Iraola.
 Read every word below, with a video of the press conference to follow:
 on Dowman's red card appeal being turned down: 
We’re very disappointed, to be fair, especially with the reckless tackles that he receives - his reaction is minimal in relation to the action. We’re disappointed it hasn’t been overturned having watched it back.
 on if it's a case of Max being punished: 
It is what it is. We’ve put every argument on the table to make a case for it - not only the action that is so evident, but when you look back in slow motion, the previous action and Max’s action is clear. Obviously, we have a very different opinion. I think you also have to look at the context of the player, the age and what happened previously.
 on if Max could've been injured badly in the challenge: 
It could have been really bad, and we’re lucky today that he hasn’t had a broken foot - that’s clear.
 Arteta's update on Saka, Madueke and Tzolis Read more on his reaction to Max being sent off: 
My reaction comes from a moment of heat and extreme frustration, because I know the consequences of that, especially for Max. It’s something that we discussed just before we went out, because it’s not the first time that happened. It happened earlier this month with England, and it will continue to happen unfortunately because of the way he plays and attracts opponents. That’s it - we need to be able to tell each other the things as they are, because he’s 16 and we need to be very protective of him, but also very straight with him at the same time with what to expect of him towards the team, individuals, and the club.
 on if everything is ok between the two of them: 
Yes, for sure. I had a talk with him yesterday; it’s just a talk. I’ve done it - so that’s why I’m so protective of these things and especially with young players, because we have made these mistakes. We know how much you can get punished, and how much it can change what happens next. It’s not the first time, so we need to put an end to it very quickly.
 on if Noni Madueke is fit: 
We don’t know yet. We’ll have a training session tomorrow, see if he can complete that full session tomorrow and as I said, I will know whether he’s available or not.
 on if he is ruling him out: 
Noni? No.
 on if Bukayo Saka will be back before the international break: 
He needed another scan to see how the amount of fluid that was there is resolving, whether the tendon is touched and how badly it is touched. Afterwards we’ll know more about it.
 on if he would rule him out of playing for England: 
Again, I don’t know. Looks like it, but we’ll have to wait and see next week.
 on when he might be back: 
We want to have him [back] as quickly as possible. The player is desperate; he’s feeling much better than he was a few days ago, and we need to wait and see how he evolves.
 on Rice, Calafiori and Tzolis: 
They all trained today, and they will train tomorrow, and if everything is ok, they will be available.
 on whether Liverpool are title challengers: 
I think all the top clubs are certainly title challengers, and it’s so early in the season, when you look at the squad, the manager that they have and the history for sure. We expect a big game on Sunday; we’re looking forward to it, for sure. It’s 14 years that we haven’t won there, so it’s time to do it.
 Quiz: Name the line-up from our 2012 Anfield win Read more on how long it has been since our last win at Anfield: 
It’s an opportunity. I came here and in many places we were 20, 22 years, 18 years without winning, and we’ve been doing all these things, so on Sunday, that’s the opportunity that we have.
 on how to keep Alexander Isak quiet: 
By keeping him as far from the goal as possible. We always try, it’s not only him, it’s all the connections that they have, especially when they have space to run. We know how dangerous they are in that kind of moment, and the quality of the striker that we are talking about. That’s the opposition in the Premier League.
 on facing Andoni Iraola: 
It’s a privilege; I think we’ve discussed that many, many times. Someone who has been your teammate, that you spent so many beautiful moments together when we were younger. To be facing each other, to be close, massive clubs in this country, in Europe, in a big match like this, it’s a blessing.
 on how Max has been since the red card: 
I mean, when you play for Arsenal, you're going to have highs and lows. You have to be prepared for that, it doesn't matter the age. So don't feel sorry for yourself; that happened, those things happened. Make sure that you are humble enough to recognise that and to learn from it and work on it. That shows you as well that there are many things that you have to be so good at to sustain the level and to maintain a certain level when you play for a club like us, and that's what he needs to do and he has the talent, he has the will and he has the capacity and the brain to do it, no question about that.
 on if he is surprised by the reaction to his reaction to Max getting sent off: 
I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it's positive or negative. But you need to understand the context, the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out. But, I don't know, you can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me, someday you'll say I don't like their reaction. For me it was the best reaction ever to be able to be who I am. But you want to always leave the best reaction and the beautiful one. You want to see the reaction of his teammates? When they have to play with 10, you want to see that? What do you expect? I don't know, and the England ones, they are his age, 16, the same. What is their reaction? That's the reaction, that's the level and that's the reaction, and whether it's right or wrong, that's the reaction, and the reaction when I don't win, you know what the reaction is? I'm pissed off, big time. So we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality. Otherwise we are in Disneyland, we are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time we are going to demand him, like to anybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Otherwise the rest of the boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair.
 on if Kai Havertz's form is related to a previous injury: 
No, there's nothing to do with that. It's true that in terms of the numbers, we have dropped those numbers but he certainly had the chances as well to play, and that kind of form and that kind of efficiency with the front players, it's very common. Full trust on him and what he's doing.
 on if Gyokeres or Havertz did enough against Fleetwood to start Sunday: 
What happened in midweek is probably the beauty of this game, and that's why people love football so much. Because when you look at what we generated, what the fans generated, you play that game 100 times, you know the results 99% of the times. But it's football and it happens, something magical and they went through. So I need to have a perspective on that, and obviously analyse but don't judge the players too hard, especially without understanding the context of it.
 How to watch Liverpool v Arsenal live on TV Read more on Noni Madueke realising his potential: 
He's getting closer but he needs to do it and he needs to make that click, and that's what the top elite players do. He has all the potential to do it, he has all the attributes to do it. He certainly has the will to do it because when you see him train every single day, he's one of the players who enjoys the practice the most and wants to expose himself to all kinds of situations and actions. Now he needs to put the performance on the pitch.
 on the opportunity he has on the right wing: 
It's actually doing it and being able to do it again, and once you do it two or three times, they will have more trust. He will have more security in what he does. He will play more minutes because, as well, sometimes we ask him to play when he's not playing regularly, and that's a bit unfair as well, and now he's got a great opportunity ahead of him.
 on if he feels Arsenal are refereed differently: 
No, I don't have that. No, and I don't have that at all. I think the players try to protect the players. I think the players, the referees study the game. They know which players are more vulnerable to bad tackles and they try to protect them. I'm sure of that and especially someone like Max, I have no doubt about that.
 on what his message was before the Fleetwood game: 
It was related to what could happen. Exactly what happened, and not only the red, the 10 seconds before, the way he comes to receive the ball, what kind of ball that is, and after that, if he gets tackled, what happens next. Exactly that.
 on if it’s a risk to play Max consistently in the first team: 
It's what it is. I think we discussed that when he made his debut in pre-season [in 2025]. We played Newcastle; it was a very physical game. That's my fear and that's why I want to protect [him]. Because if a player who weighs 95kg, 100kg, comes at 35km/h to Max and hits a bone, I don't know what happens. So when we talk about protecting him, the week before you were asking me why he's not playing every week when he's done really well against Everton. So we really need to put some perspective in every context of the player that we have, which is tremendous, and leave it there, and let him grow and let's protect him. All of us.
 on if patience is needed with Max: 
I don't think it needs reminding; that's the reality. Otherwise we live in a different reality. I think we discussed a week ago how many players in the history of the Premier League have done what Max is doing, and there isn't one. So it's something new, and as it's new, I will do things well; I will do things not so well. I will try to learn as quickly as possible, protect him as much as possible. But at the same time, it's the level that we are in, and we are here to win football matches and to perform at the highest level.
 When Arsenal and Liverpool started a TV tradition Read more on how he can use his experience as a player to get a win at Anfield: 
Well, going there with full conviction, that's number one, and we've been very, very close in the last few years to win. But something is missing, and that's what we've been discussing the last few days. To go there with a real purpose. To hurt them and get away from there with a victory.
 on how to get through Liverpool's 'chaos': 
Those chaotic moments can come from situations where you have a clear advantage to play and other ones that you don't have any advantage and you have to play a different game. We are both teams very aggressive in our high press, not giving any time to the opponent. I know Andoni really well. So we're both going to face a lot of moments that are very similar, and to escape or to break that, it will be important. But it will be not the only aspect that it's relevant to win the game.
